findings.title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never removes the WorkflowReminder row
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns early without deleting (or flagging) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers that previously deleted the row themselves no longer do (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` for the original rescheduled booking). The result is rows left behind with `scheduled: true` and a referenceId that has already been cancelled; they linger until the cron's `deleteMany(scheduledDate <= now)` cleanup, and the cron's `cancelled` sweep will never touch them. At minimum this is stale data for reporting/queries; it also makes the semantics of the function inconsistent with the `!referenceId` branch, which does delete the row.

findings.title: Cancellation sweep does not filter by method and aborts all remaining cancellations on first error
findings.body: `remindersToCancel` queries only `cancelled: true` without `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, so any non-email reminder that ever gets flagged cancelled will have its Twilio SID posted to the SendGrid `scheduled_sends` endpoint. More importantly the whole `for` loop is inside a single try/catch: if one SendGrid request fails (invalid/expired batch id, rate limit), the loop exits and every remaining reminder in this run is left uncancelled, so their emails may be sent before the next cron tick (the window is only 1 hour while the cron runs every 15 min, so a couple of failed runs is enough to leak reminders). Each reminder should be cancelled/deleted in its own try/catch and the query should be scoped to EMAIL.

findings.title: SendGrid client API key is never set in this handler
findings.body: `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called at module load, but `client` (`@sendgrid/client`) has no `client.setApiKey(...)` call in this file, unlike `emailReminderManager.ts` which does both. The new cancellation requests (and the existing `/v3/mail/batch` call) therefore go out unauthenticated and will fail with 401, meaning cancelled reminders are never actually cancelled — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: try/catch cannot catch failures from async reminder deletions
findings.body: `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` invokes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting; the returned promises escape the surrounding try/catch. Although both helpers swallow their own errors internally today, any throw outside their try (or a future change) becomes an unhandled rejection rather than the logged error the code intends. The same pattern exists in `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx`; consider `await Promise.all(...)`.

findings.title: SMS reminder row is not deleted if twilio.cancelSMS throws
findings.body: `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` share one try block. If cancelling fails (e.g. the message already left the queue, or a transient Twilio error), the DB row is never deleted and the reminder stays in the table indefinitely with `scheduled: true`. Deleting the row should be done regardless of the cancel result.

findings.title: Malformed import (missing trailing comma) and type-only imports converted to value imports
findings.body: The import block now reads `  TimeUnit,\n  Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";` with no trailing comma and inconsistent formatting, which will fail the repo's prettier/lint check. Additionally `Prisma` and `PrismaPromise` were switched from `import type` to value imports here (and `App`/`Credential`/`EventTypeCustomInput`/`Prisma` in `handleNewBooking.ts`), which pulls type-only symbols into the runtime import graph unnecessarily.
